author: Ted Black
title: St. Mary's County girls lacrosse players earn All-American honors - NewsBreak
text:
By Ted Black ,
19 hours ago
Although they have already garnered their high school diplomas and begun to set a course for their college days ahead later this summer, a quartet of St. Mary’s County girls lacrosse players were able to add more accolades to their resumes last week when they earned All-American recognition from USA Lacrosse.
St. Mary’s Ryken High School graduate Macey Bowles and Leonardtown High graduates Alaina “Ally” Burks, the SMAC girls lacrosse player of the year last spring, both earned All-American honors for their efforts on the field.
Burks, along with fellow Leonardtown graduates Clara Hammett and Julia Lisa, all earned All-Academic designation from USA Lacrosse.
“I was very surprised when I heard that I had been selected,” said Burks, who is headed to Stevens University for women’s lacrosse. “I had heard something about All-American selections when I was a freshman, but I hadn’t really given it much thought. But it’s an honor to be selected. It shows that all the hard work paid off.”
In addition to their All-American status, the quartet also honed their skills from a very young age through high school playing club lacrosse for the Southern Maryland Jets, overseen by Leonardtown girls’ coach Cynthia Lisa. Fittingly, during the same spring in which her players were selected for All-American honors, Lisa was tabbed as the coach of the year.
“These awards are always an honor, but they’re really about the players,” Lisa said. “I wouldn’t be in position to win games and win a coaching award if it were not for these players. I have a great staff of seven coaches and these young ladies have always put in the hard work that it takes on the field and in the classroom.”
Burks, Hammett and Lisa were all part of the Raiders’ success the past four years which culminated with a trip to the Maryland 4A State championship game last month where Leonardtown suffered a tough, 8-6 setback to Urbana. Burks led the team with 55 goals during the season and tallied four in the losing cause in the state tile game, while Hammett and Lisa both played key supporting roles all season.
“It was such an amazing experience to be part of the team with these girls all four years,” said Hammett, who is headed to Gannon College for women’s lacrosse this fall. “We’ve all been playing together with Jets since we were like 5 or 6 years old. Then to be able to have the last four years together at Leonardtown and play in the state championship game was a great experience.”
Bowles, who is headed to Xavier University for women’s lacrosse, may have traveled a different route from her Jets’ teammates once she began playing high school lacrosse at St. Mary’s Ryken, but she was also part of a solid Knights’ squad last spring that reached the WCAC semifinals.
“I always loved playing with this group of girls on Jets,” Bowles said. “We always had great players and great coaches and it was a fun experience. I’m a very competitive person, so I wanted my senior year at Ryken to be special. We had a lot of drama early on, but then we got it together during the season and we went further than anyone expected. We made it to [WCAC] semifinals which no one expected.”
